newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer expects full-year 97 earnings to rise.
newsitem.headline: Bayer expects full-year 97 earnings to rise.

text.p: German chemicals and pharmaceutical group Bayer AG on Tuesday reaffirmed its forecast for 1997 sales to top 50 billion marks ($27.3 billion), after it reported earnings in line with analysts' forecasts.
Bayer, the last of the so-called 'Big Three' among German chemical companies to report its first-half results, also said it was confident net earnings in the full-year would rise.
"For the second half of the year we are confident that lively demand will continue while foreign exchange rates will stabilise," the group said in a statement.
"As such we are confident that we can report sales of 50 billion marks for the full year and full-year net profit above the previous year," Bayer said.
Net profit rose 13 percent to 1.7 billion marks, while group sales increased 11 percent to 27.4 billion marks in the first six months of the year.
Sales had been expected to rise to somewhere between 26.5 billion and 26.9 billion marks from 24.80 billion marks in the year-ago period, marking an advance of between 6.9 and 8.1 percent.
In common with other major German exporters, Bayer reaped the benefits of the stronger dollar which made its products cheaper abroad.

Bayer said 1.3 billion marks of the 2.6 billion mark increase in sales was attributable to exchange rates, 1.7 billion to higher volumes and 300 million marks to newly acquired business. An unsatisfactory price trend diminished the sales figures by 700 million marks.
"The greatest stimulus to growth came from our companies outside Europe, which recorded seven percent higher sales overall," Bayer said.
"In the second quarter, however, our German companies also showed a substantial improvement."
The increase in group sales was driven mainly by the continuing upward business trend in the Americas, Bayer said.
Operating profit rose six percent to three billion marks, while group cash flow was up 18 percent at 3.2 billion marks in the first half.

Group pre-tax profit was 2.8 billion marks in the first half of 1997, a rise of 2.5 percent. Analysts polled by Reuters expected Bayer to post pre-tax profit of between 2.8 and 2.86 billion marks, an increase of between 2.6 and five percent.
Shares in Bayer were on a rollercoaster ride in early trade, falling nearly two percent at one stage only to recover after the figures were published.
The shares were up two marks, or 2.85 percent, at 70 marks by 1020 GMT, while the overall DAX index was up 2.3 percent to 4,172.28.
